mcqs.q: In this barn-fire evacuation study of dairy cattle, what had the greatest impact on the animals' readiness to leave the familiar housing?
o: Adapting the exits to the cattle's sensory physiology
mcqs.e: Tailoring exit design to cattle sensory physiology produced an extensive effect, making even non-habituated cattle evacuate quickly.

mcqs.q: The preliminary assumption that pasture-trained cattle would have a decisive evacuation advantage was:
o: Not supported — exit design mattered more
mcqs.e: Cattle not habituated to the adapted exit still evacuated quickly, contradicting the assumed advantage of training.

mcqs.q: Which measures were used to assess stress in the evacuated cattle?
o: Faecal cortisol metabolites and daily milk yield
mcqs.e: Stress was assessed via faecal cortisol metabolites and daily milk yield alongside evacuation time.

mcqs.q: According to this report, emergency response for aquatic companion animals during wildfires:
o: Is identical to terrestrial animal response
mcqs.e: The report emphasizes that aquatic animal evacuation and housing pose unique logistic challenges distinct from terrestrial animals.

mcqs.q: Veterinarians who become familiar with aquatic animal evacuation and care before a wildfire response can:
o: Extend the scope of disaster recovery
mcqs.e: Prior familiarity with aquatic animal care lets veterinarians extend disaster-recovery capabilities.

mcqs.q: On measures of psychological health, veterinary and animal care workers in this Black Summer bushfire study scored:
o: Highly on measures of psychological ill-health
mcqs.e: Overall participants scored highly on PTSD symptoms, distress, burnout and grief.

mcqs.q: A key limitation acknowledged by the authors was:
o: Cross-sectional design and non-probability sampling limiting generalisability
mcqs.e: The cross-sectional, non-probability (Facebook/email) recruitment limited generalisability and risked response bias.

mcqs.q: Across domestic violence, homelessness, and natural disasters, a prominent outcome for companion animals during forced separation was:
o: Death and loss of the animals
mcqs.e: Death and loss of animals were prominent across all three categories of forced separation.

mcqs.q: To avoid forced separation from their pets, people in the review were reported to:
o: Delay fleeing abuse and prolong homelessness awaiting pet-friendly housing
mcqs.e: Risks taken included failing to evacuate, delaying escape from abuse, and prolonged homelessness while waiting for pet-friendly accommodation.

mcqs.q: Two major themes that emerged from the review were:
o: Cost of care and breed preference
Responsibility for the animal and the belief in human superiority over animals
mcqs.e: Responsibility for the animal and the cultural belief in human wellbeing as superior to animal wellbeing were major themes.

mcqs.q: Compared with mother-reared kittens, orphaned hand-reared kittens showed:
o: No detectable difference in telomere length
mcqs.e: No detectable telomere-length differences were found by orphan status, survival, or time point.

mcqs.q: The study concluded that early maternal separation in domestic kittens:
o: Did not accelerate telomere shortening in the first months of life
mcqs.e: Early maternal separation with subsequent hand-rearing did not accelerate telomere shortening through 2 months of age.

mcqs.q: Compared with 2019 puppies, 'Pandemic Puppies' acquired in 2020 were:
o: More likely to attend puppy training classes
Less likely to attend puppy training classes
mcqs.e: Only 28.9% of Pandemic Puppies attended classes versus 67.9% of 2019 puppies.

mcqs.q: Pandemic Puppies were significantly more likely than 2019 puppies to be:
o: Examined by a vet before purchase
mcqs.e: Designer Crossbreeds rose from 18.8% to 26.1%, while KC registration and pre-purchase vet checks fell.

mcqs.q: The authors concluded that this cohort of puppies will likely need:
o: Greater veterinary and behavioural professional support
mcqs.e: Greater veterinary and behavioural support is needed to ameliorate health and behavioural impacts of growing up in the pandemic.

mcqs.q: What limitation did the authors emphasize about their dentition-timeline findings?
o: Too many breeds confounded the results
Only two dogs of one breed, so results cannot be generalized
The exact birth date was unknown
mcqs.e: Only two Yorkshire Terrier puppies were studied, so observations cannot be generalized.

mcqs.q: The first teeth to erupt (at about 4.5 weeks of age) were the:
o: Canines together with the adjacent incisors (i3)
mcqs.e: Canines and the adjacent i3 incisors appeared first at 4.5 weeks; i1 came later.

mcqs.q: After the interactive dog-bite-prevention program, preschool children's questionnaire scores:
mcqs.e: Significant improvements were seen on both questionnaires after the education program.

mcqs.q: Regarding age, the study found that:
o: Older students scored significantly higher, so age should be considered in program design
mcqs.e: Older students scored higher, suggesting age should guide bite-prevention program design.

mcqs.q: The 'Being a Tree' concept was:
o: Too difficult for any age group
Successfully learned by children across all age groups
mcqs.e: 'Being a Tree' was learnable across all ages, making it a useful universal component.

mcqs.q: Which zoonotic agent had the highest seroprevalence in these free-roaming cats?
mcqs.e: T. gondii seroprevalence was 42%, above C. burnetii (37%) and C. felis (8%).

mcqs.q: Coxiella burnetii seropositivity was correlated with:
o: Percentage of urban areas and human population size
mcqs.e: C. burnetii correlated with urban/peri-urban areas and human population size, unlike T. gondii (orchards).

mcqs.q: Adult cats were significantly more likely than young cats to be seropositive for:
mcqs.e: Adults had higher odds (OR 2.3) of C. burnetii seropositivity; no age difference for the others.

mcqs.q: Seropositivity for ectoparasitic (vector-borne) diseases in the screened pets:
o: Was much higher among unhoused owners' pets
Did not vary by housing status
Was higher among housed owners' pets
mcqs.e: Seropositivity of ectoparasitic diseases did not differ between housed and unhoused owners' pets.

mcqs.q: What proportion of owners said they would NOT give up their pet for better housing?
mcqs.e: Across groups, 96–98% stated they would not relinquish their pet for better housing.

mcqs.q: Compared with housed owners, unhoused owners were significantly more likely to report:
o: Finding a flea on their pet and challenges obtaining housing
mcqs.e: Unhoused owners more often reported fleas, housing challenges, bottled-water use, and co-sleeping.

mcqs.q: Among unhoused participants, past-year care-seeking was:
o: Higher for themselves than for their pets
Higher for their pets (93%) than for themselves (86%)
mcqs.e: 93% sought veterinary care for pets versus 86% seeking care for themselves.

mcqs.q: To reduce barriers to care for unhoused pet owners, the authors recommend:
o: Banning pet ownership among the homeless
Integrated One Health (human and animal) interprofessional services
mcqs.e: An integrated One Health clinic model can leverage the human-animal bond to improve access for both.

mcqs.q: Self-described health status in the study showed:
mcqs.e: 90% of pets were rated healthy/very healthy versus only 47% of owners.

mcqs.q: When a person requesting financial assistance was accompanied by a pet, participants expressed:
mcqs.e: Pet presence reduced suspicion and, among those low in social justice orientation, increased concern and giving.

mcqs.q: Greater support for policies that enable pet care among people in poverty was associated with:
o: Higher social justice orientation and positive attitudes toward animals
mcqs.e: Social justice orientation and attitudes toward animals predicted support for enabling (not restricting) policies.

mcqs.q: Making the benefits of the human-pet relationship salient:
o: Increased support among those lower in social justice orientation or less empathetic toward animals
mcqs.e: Salient benefit cues raised support for enabling policies among otherwise less-compassionate individuals.
